This is manifestly not what Adorno had in mind. His ‘fetishization’ of music is, properly speaking, the systematic commodification of music, which presumably subsumes its use value ‘as music’ to its exchange value. en: 1 The ‘Aura’ of a Work of Art

children: 本雅明在《机械复制时代的艺术作品》中写道：
In
The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction
, Benjamin observed that:
对艺术作品的技术复制是……贯穿整个历史、断断续续进行着的事情，间隔很长，强度却不断增加。希腊人只有两种技术复制艺术作品的工艺：铸造和压印。青铜器、陶器和铸币是他们能够大量制造的唯一几类艺术品。其余一切都是独一无二的，无法用技术手段复制。

Technological reproduction of the work of art is something … that has been practised intermittently throughout history, at widely separated intervals though with growing intensity. The Greeks had only two processes for reproducing works of art technologically: casting and embossing. Bronzes, terracottas and coins were the only artworks that they were able to manufacture in large numbers. All the rest were unique and not capable of being reproduced by technological means.
众所周知，本雅明的这一观察涉及艺术作品的独一性、本真性，即“灵光”（aura），也就是“自作品诞生以来一切可传承之物的精髓，从它的物质存续到它所承载的历史见证”。
艺术作品的“灵光”深深植根于作品所嵌入的传统，与它的仪式功能不可分离。从历史上看，围绕艺术作品的仪式最初当然是膜拜性的（巫术的或宗教的）。但艺术作品也附着一种世俗仪式，本雅明称之为“对美的侍奉”。
随着文艺复兴到来，世俗的、即非宗教的一面开始从膜拜中脱离出来，逐渐接管了全部仪式功能。

Benjamin’s observation, as is well known, relates to the singularity, genuineness, or ‘aura’, of a work of art, i.e. to the ‘quintessence of everything about it since its creation that can be handed down, from its material duration to the historical witness that it bears’.

The ‘aura’ of a work of art is very much part of the tradition into which the work is embedded, and is inseparable from its ritual function. Historically, the ritual that surrounds a work of art has, of course, been cultic (magical or religious) in the first instance. But there has also been a secular ritual attached to works of art, which Benjamin calls ‘the service of beauty’.
With the Renaissance, the secular, or profane, aspect began to detach itself from the cultic, gradually taking over the ritual function altogether.
在本雅明看来，“灵光”的终结伴随着发达资本主义内部真正革命性的复制能力的出现。如果艺术作品能够轻易地大量复制，艺术就会摆脱对仪式的依赖。作品的“灵光”将被机械复制摧毁：

For Benjamin, the end of ‘aura’ came with the emergence of truly revolutionary capabilities of reproduction within advanced capitalism. If works of art could be reproduced easily and in high volume, then art would be freed from reliance on ritual. The ‘aura’ of the work would be destroyed by mechanical reproduction:
大体可以说，复制技术把被复制之物从传统的领域中移了出来。它制作大量复制品，以众多的显现取代了独一无二的显现。它让复制品逼近接受者所处的任何情境，从而使被复制之物现实化。
Reproductive technology, we might say in general terms, removes the thing

reproduced from the realm of tradition. In making many copies of the reproduction, it substitutes for its unique incidence a multiplicity of incidences. And in allowing the reproduction to come closer to whatever situation the person apprehends it is in, it actualizes what is reproduced.

“灵光”的摧毁意味着艺术作品“展示”价值的胜利和宗教或膜拜价值的消失，这在摄影和电影上表现得十分明显。然而不止如此，“灵光”的摧毁还改变了“大众”与艺术的关系。机械复制的艺术作品逼近“大众”，改变了“大众”对艺术欣赏的参与方式。诚然，“大众”倾向于以“消遣”（distracted）的方式吸收艺术，而不是“凝神观照”它，但反复的接触即使在“心不在焉”的人中间也会养成占有艺术的习惯。毕竟，在历史大动荡的时代，直接的凝神观照不足以把握艺术。“大众”还必须“习惯于”艺术作品，作为能动的参与者进入占有过程，哪怕“心不在焉”，就像他们作为电影观众时那样。于是，政治成了“大众”借以占有艺术的场域。

The destruction of the ‘aura’ entails the triumph of the ‘display’ value of a work of art and the disappearance of religious or cultic value, as is apparent for photography and film. More than that, however, the destruction of the ‘aura’ changes the relationship of the ‘masses’ to art. A mechanically reproduced work of art comes closer to the ‘masses’ and changes the participation of the ‘masses’ in appreciating art. To be sure, the ‘masses’ tend to absorb art in a ‘distracted’ manner, rather than by ‘contemplating’ it,

but repeated exposure creates the habit of appropriating art even among the ‘distracted’. Direct contemplation, after all, is not enough to apprehend art at times of great historical upheaval. It is also necessary for the ‘masses’ to ‘get used’ to works of art and to operate as active participants in the process of appropriation, even if ‘distracted’, as when they are the audience of film. Thus, politics becomes the terrain through which art is appropriated by the ‘masses’.
重访这块文化与艺术理论的神圣——也是被人踩烂了的——地盘，起因是本雅明一句随口的话：铸币是一件艺术作品，而且是一件自历史深处以来其“灵光”就遭受机械复制破坏性影响的艺术作品。本雅明的观察乍看无可指摘，因为它指的是古希腊铸币。但其他铸币呢？这个问题一经提出，别的问题便接踵而来：银行券呢？信用卡呢？如此等等。究竟是不是货币——而不只是铸币——在某种深刻意义上就是艺术？

The reason for revisiting this hallowed – and much-trodden – ground of cultural and art theory is Benjamin’s throwaway remark that coin is a work of art, and moreover one whose ‘aura’ has been subjected to the destructive influence of mechanical reproduction since the depths of historical time. Benjamin’s observation appears unobjectionable at first sight, as it refers to ancient Greek coins. But what about other coinage? Once that question is asked, others naturally follow: What about banknotes? And credit cards? And so on. Indeed, is it really money rather than simply coin that is art in some profound sense?
再者，如果货币确有艺术之维，这能否照亮本雅明所处理的那个问题本身，即随着资本主义关系逐渐支配社会，艺术作品所发生的转型？铸币确实已被机械复制了数千年，这是它本性中固有的特征。但在资本主义世界里，货币已从金属圆片变为纸条，变为账簿条目，变为电子信号。货币及其材料的转型，能否为理解资本主义关系伸入社会与私人生活新领域之际艺术作品的转型提供启示？货币的转型与艺术和“大众”的关系又有何干系？

Moreover, if money does have an artistic dimension, would that shed any light on the very issue that Benjamin came to grips with, namely the transformation of the work of art as capitalist relations have gradually come to dominate society? Coin has indeed been mechanically reproduced for millennia, a feature that is inherent to its nature. But in the capitalist world, money has been transformed from metallic disc, to strip of paper, to book entry, to electronic signal. Does the transformation of money and its material offer any insight into the transformation of artworks as capitalist relations have ramified into new areas of social and private life? And does the transformation of money have any bearing on the relationship between art and the ‘masses’?

不过，在回答这些问题之前，先简短地看一下阿多诺的《论音乐中的拜物教性质与听觉的退化》是有益的。正如伯恩斯坦在《文化工业》导言中所说，这篇文章最好被看作对本雅明那篇文章的论战。阿多诺含蓄地拒绝了艺术作品拥有被机械复制摧毁的“灵光”这一观念：资本主义关系渗入艺术世界，对“大众”把握艺术的方式有着十分不同的意涵。阿多诺的论证围绕“音乐拜物教”展开，其极端表现是音乐被商业性地用作其他活动的背景。“严肃”音乐远不能免于此种命运，连贝多芬和巴赫也可能遭殃。在阿多诺看来，这是马克思的“商品拜物教”侵蚀音乐的结果。他写道：

Before engaging with these questions, however, it is instructive briefly to turn to Adorno’s ‘On the Fetish Character in Music and the Regression of Listening’, which, as Bernstein comments in the introduction to The Culture Industry,

is best regarded as a polemic against Benjamin’s essay. Adorno implicitly rejected the notion that the work of art has an ‘aura’ that is destroyed by mechanical reproduction: the penetration of the art world by capitalist relations has very different implications for the apprehension of art by the ‘masses’. Adorno’s argument pivoted on ‘musical fetishism’, witnessed in the extreme through the commercial use of music as background to other activities. ‘Serious’ music is far from immune to this fate, which could befall even Beethoven and Bach. For Adorno, this is the result of Marx’s ‘commodity fetishism’ subverting music. Thus:
如果说商品一般而言是交换价值与使用价值的结合，那么，在完全资本主义化的社会中，文化商品必须保住其纯粹使用价值的假象，而这种纯粹使用价值就必定被纯粹交换价值所取代——后者恰恰以其交换价值的身份，欺骗性地接管了使用价值的功能。音乐特有的拜物教性质就在于这种偷梁换柱。

If the commodity in general combines exchange value and use value, then the pure use value, whose illusion the cultural goods must preserve in a completely capitalist society, must be replaced by pure exchange value, which precisely in its capacity as exchange value deceptively takes over the function of use value. The specific fetish character of music lies in this quid pro quo.
去听托斯卡尼尼音乐会的人“实际上崇拜的是他自己为门票付出的钱”。
交换价值成了艺术享受的对象；随着交换价值支配并摧毁对人的使用价值，这一过程越来越不可阻挡。
带来快感的是购买行为，而不是艺术对象本身——这是一种败坏音乐品质的拜物教。
The person who goes to a Toscanini concert ‘is really worshipping the money that he himself has paid for the ticket’.
Exchange value has become the object of artistic enjoyment, a process that is ever more inexorable as exchange value dominates and destroys use values for human beings.
It is the act of buying that offers the pleasure, not the art object per se, a fetishism that degrades the quality of music.
在阿多诺看来，随着资本渗入社会并按自己的号令塑造社会，使用价值被归摄于交换价值之下，艺术因此被拜物教化，因为它的文化（和艺术）使用价值被交换价值取代了。这一过程构成了文化工业的基础；文化工业是一种均质化力量，抹去艺术的特殊性，制造出普遍的低劣趣味。艺术价值的丧失，对应着消费这种艺术的“大众”的文化贫困。于是，听“拜物教化”的音乐就会“退化”，停滞在“婴儿阶段”。
音乐越是屈从于机械复制——尤其在广告中——这种“退化”就越带上“强制性质”。
为“大众”按资本主义方式生产出来的流行音乐的出现，远没有把音乐引向进步的方向，反而既贬低了音乐，也贬低了“大众”。

For Adorno, as capital penetrates society and shapes it according to its own dictates, use value is subsumed under exchange value, and thus art is fetishised because its cultural (and artistic) use value comes to be replaced by exchange value. This process lies at the foundations of the culture industry, which is a homogenising force that eliminates the particularity of art and produces a universal outlook of debasement. The loss of artistic value corresponds to the cultural impoverishment of the ‘masses’ that consume such art. Listening to ‘fetishized’ music thus ‘regresses’ and is arrested at ‘an infantile stage’.
The more that music submits to mechanical reproduction, particularly in advertising, the more that ‘regression’ assumes a ‘compulsory character’.
Far from transforming music in a progressive direction, the emergence of popular music, produced capitalistically for the ‘masses’, degrades both music and the ‘masses’.
这就是阿多诺区分“高级”与“低级”艺术的基础，更不用说他的如下看法：资本对文化的支配消灭了特殊之物，摧毁了对资本的反抗。在艺术与“大众”的关系、以及交换价值对个人的掌控这两个问题上，他与本雅明的对立十分尖锐。货币很早就遭受机械复制，它能否为这些问题提供启示？

This was the foundation of Adorno’s view of the distinction between ‘high’ and ‘low’ art, not to mention his opinion that the domination of culture by capital eliminates the particular and destroys opposition to capital. The contrast with Benjamin regarding the relation of art to the ‘masses’ and the hold of exchange value on individuals is sharp. Could money, which has been subjected to mechanical reproduction from an early stage, shed any light on these issues?

zh: 2 货币作为一种艺术形式
en: 2 Money as a Form of Art

children: 货币构成一种艺术形式吗？就古希腊铸币而言，本雅明似乎毫不怀疑；任何走进雅典钱币博物馆的人也不得不同意。希腊铸币以其全部银质华美，陈列在那座新古典主义宅邸的各个展厅里——它最初是恩斯特·齐勒为海因里希·施利曼建造的，后者正是发掘特洛伊、继而发掘迈锡尼的人。身处艺术面前的感觉是直接而强烈的。然而，一般而言的货币远早于铸币，在历史进程中采取过若干其他形式。例如在衡量价值时，荷马时代的货币是牛，非洲努尔人当中至今仍是如此。古希腊铸币也许是艺术，但无论怎么努力，都很难看出一群牛的艺术价值。银行账户和计算机条目的艺术面向又可能是什么呢？

Does money constitute a form of art? Benjamin appeared to be in no doubt as far as ancient Greek coins were concerned, and anyone who has walked into the Numismatic Museum of Athens could not but concur. Greek coinage in all its silver magnificence is displayed in the rooms of the neoclassical residence originally built by Ernst Ziller for Heinrich Schliemann, the man who dug Troy and then Mycenae. The sense of being in the presence of art is immediate and gripping. Yet money in general has long predated coinage, taking several other forms in the course of history. When it comes to measuring value, for instance, money was oxen in Homer,
and so it still remains among the Nuer of Africa.
Ancient Greek coins were perhaps art but, try as one might, it is hard to identify the artistic value of a herd of cattle. And what might be the artistic aspect of bank accounts and computer entries?

更仔细地考察希腊铸币，或许能找到答案；尤其因为再想一想，它们作为艺术的性质远非一目了然。一枚雅典四德拉克马银币——一只猫头鹰，或者更典型地，一枚埃伊纳斯塔特银币——一只龟，无疑是精美绝伦的工艺制品。但它们是艺术作品吗？就单个物件而言，只有把“艺术”一词的外延推到极限，答案才会是肯定的。不过，想想面对大量希腊铸币时会发生什么，尤其是币型也多种多样时。在雅典钱币博物馆的展厅里，形形色色的铸币琳琅满目，承载着丰富的图像，艺术的存在无可争辩。参观者被一个由神祇、英雄、象征性图像和铭文交织而成的整体所包围，一切以银精细呈现。单独一只雅典猫头鹰算不上艺术，而一套古典希腊银币却显然像是艺术。希腊铸币以相当数量汇聚在一起时，其艺术品质清晰显现；单独考察时，其艺术身份却远不明显。

An answer to this question could be found by considering Greek coins more closely, particularly as, on further reflection, their nature as art is far from straightforward. An Athenian tetradrachm, an owl, or even more, an individual Aeginetan stater, a tortoise, are without question craft objects of exquisite beauty. But are they works of art? Seen as individual objects, the answer would be in the affirmative only if one were prepared to stretch the meaning of art to breaking point. Consider though what happens when one is confronted with a large number of Greek coins, especially if there is also variety of type. In the rooms of the Numismatic Museum of Athens, with their profusion of different coins bearing a wealth of representations, the presence of art is indisputable. The visitor is surrounded by a veritable matrix of gods, heroes, symbolic images and inscriptions, depicted delicately in silver. An Athenian owl by itself is hardly art, and yet a set of classical Greek silver coins most certainly appears to be. When Greek coins are put together in significant numbers, their artistic quality emerges clearly, but when they are considered individually, their status as art is far from obvious.

那么，是什么赋予一套希腊铸币艺术品质？材料无疑重要，银工的精细也重要。然而稍加思索就会明白，把希腊铸币变成艺术的，并不是它们的魅力与美。事实上，其艺术内容的来源更深，与这些铸币曾经实际执行货币职能这一事实相关。因为如果观察者不知道这些物件曾是货币，图像依旧精美，材料依旧闪光，但物件就成了空洞无物的银片，也许是某人的愚行。而当观察者意识到这些物件古代的“货币性”（moneyness）时，它们唤起观念与情感的力量就变得巨大。由此直接可知：本雅明视为当然的希腊铸币的艺术面向，植根于它们的“货币性”，图像与材料之美反而是次要的。它们的艺术内容在成套展示时更容易被把握，因为成套展示让铸币集体的“货币性”更容易作为可触的社会与历史事实显现出来。

What, then, gives to a set of Greek coins their artistic quality? The material is undoubtedly important, as is the delicacy of the silverwork. However, a moment’s reflection would show that it is not the charm and beauty of Greek coins that turns them into art. Indeed, the source of their artistic content is deeper and related to the fact that the coins once actively functioned as money. For if the observer were not aware of these objects having been money, the images would have remained delicate and the material would have continued to glisten, but the objects would have been plain silver discs devoid of content, perhaps someone’s folly. Yet when the observer is aware of the objects’ ancient ‘moneyness’, their power to connote ideas and sentiments becomes enormous. It follows immediately that the artistic aspect of Greek coins, which Benjamin took for granted, is rooted in their ‘moneyness’, while the beauty of the images and of the material is of secondary importance. Their artistic content is easier to apprehend in large sets which make it easier for the collective ‘moneyness’ of coins to appear as a tangible social and historical fact.

更具体地说，每个希腊城邦都力图通过铸币的图像与材料，传达其公民自豪感、宗教信仰、力量以及它对美的理解。正因为两千年后的观察者仍意识到“货币性”，铸币才能符号化希腊城邦对自身的认知，从而构建出整个希腊世界的图景——同质，却又高度个体化。一套希腊铸币以符号方式重现已逝世界的力量、宗教信仰、仪式，以及赤裸裸的商业贪欲。希腊人的统一与纷争，很少像在雅典钱币博物馆的展厅里那样被捕捉得淋漓尽致。这怎能不是高级的艺术？

To be more specific, each Greek city-state strove to convey something of its civic pride, its religious beliefs, its power, and its perception of beauty through the images and the material of its coins. Because the observer is aware of ‘moneyness’ even two millennia later, the coins are capable of symbolising the perception that Greek city-states had of themselves, thereby constructing a picture of the Hellenic world as a whole, homogeneous and yet highly individualistic. A set of Greek coins recreates symbolically the power, religious beliefs, rituals, and plain commercial cupidity of a long-lost world. Rarely has the unity and the fractiousness of the Greeks been better captured than in the rooms of the Numismatic Museum of Athens. How could this not be art of a high order?

由此可见，货币确有内在的艺术之维，它在希腊铸币的精美形式中被直接把握。这一艺术之维植根于“货币性”本身——尤其是植根于货币符号化关系、做法与制度的能力——而不是货币特定形式的美。正如后文各节所讨论的，“货币性”是纯粹交换价值的表象，是购买能力的化身，它抓住了社会内部与社会之间商业关系的本质。这是一种枯燥的本质，不含其他规定性，因此在符号化其他关系——包括社会与政治权力关系——时可以高度柔韧。这就是货币艺术价值的根源。

It thus appears that money does have an intrinsic artistic dimension which is immediately apprehended in the exquisite form of Greek coins. This artistic dimension is rooted in ‘moneyness’ itself – above all, in money’s ability to symbolise relations, practices and institutions – rather than in the beauty of money’s particular forms. As is discussed in subsequent sections, ‘moneyness’ is a representation of pure exchange value, the embodiment of the ability to buy, which captures the essence of commercial relations within and among societies. It is a dull essence, devoid of other determinations, and hence it can be highly pliable in symbolising other relations, including those of social and political power. This is the root of money’s artistic value.
但是，如果货币因其“货币性”而非特定形式之美而具有艺术面向，那么直接可知：银行账户、支票和电子货币也有艺术之维。货币的材料对货币作为艺术作品当然并非无关紧要，但无论是材料还是货币特定形式的美学之美，都不真正决定它的艺术身份。货币的艺术之维纯粹来自它是货币。照此看来，在努尔人眼中，一群牛大概确有艺术价值。毕竟，努尔人似乎正是通过牛获得自我感，并发展彼此之间以及与神的关系——人与牛“是一体的”。
这个惊人的结论，以及货币形式在资本主义社会中演化时浮现的复杂意涵，将在本章其余部分讨论。但首先有必要从目的与功能的角度，更深入地考察货币的艺术面向。

But if money has an artistic aspect because of its ‘moneyness’ rather than the beauty of its particular forms, it follows immediately that bank accounts, cheques and electronic money also have an artistic dimension. The material of money is certainly not irrelevant to money as a work of art, but neither the material nor the aesthetic beauty of money’s particular forms actually determine its status as art. Money’s artistic dimension derives purely from being money. By this token, a herd of cattle probably does have artistic value in the eyes of the Nuer. After all, it seems that, through their cattle, the Nuer acquire a sense of self as well as developing relations among themselves and with the divine – people and cattle ‘are one’.

This startling conclusion and the complex implications that emerge as the form of money evolves in a capitalist society are discussed in the rest of the chapter. But first it is necessary to delve a little deeper into money’s artistic aspect, considering it in terms of purpose and function.
货币当然不是作为艺术作品被生产出来的。
毋宁说，货币“机械复制”的目的是创造一般等价物，即商业经济中的购买、支付与贮藏手段。艺术很少与如此平庸的动机相联系，也很少与如此粗鄙、如此麻木的功能相联系。商业行为与以商业上适足的形式表现价值，并非艺术精神的天然居所。即使货币被明确生产出来以彰显国家权力，那几乎不加掩饰的暴力和国家的任意特权，也很难构成艺术的沃土。于是，货币的艺术内容似乎是出于完全不同的原因而被生产之物的一种偶然属性。
Money is certainly not produced as a work of art.

Rather, the purpose of the ‘mechanical reproduction’ of money is to create the universal equivalent, i.e. the means of purchase, payment and hoarding in a commercial economy. Rarely could art be associated with a more pedestrian motive, nor with functions of a crasser and more insensitive disposition. The acts of commerce and the representation of value in a commercially adequate form are not a natural abode for the artistic spirit. Even when money is produced explicitly to project state power, the thinly veiled violence and the arbitrary prerogatives of the state hardly constitute a propitious terrain for art. The artistic content of money thus appears to be an accidental feature of a thing that is produced for entirely different reasons.

然而再想一想，货币这一表面悖谬的面向恰恰证明了它的艺术本性。因为正如本雅明所见，艺术作品在历史上从来与其他功能不可分离，那些功能往往是巫术的或宗教的。文艺复兴为艺术的世俗功能的胜利开辟了道路，而资本主义关系对社会的支配则带来了艺术作品仪式或膜拜价值的最终消亡。艺术变得非宗教化，与其他功能脱离，连它的仪式也大体世俗化了。然而货币从未经历那种在晚期资本主义中成为艺术典型特征的职能分离。事实上，货币不可能“作为艺术”被生产出来而仍然是货币，因为它的艺术面向是其运行的不可分割的部分，源自它的“货币性”。正因如此，货币是艺术原始形式的返祖；它是一个逝去时代的奇特遗物。

On further reflection, however, even this ostensibly paradoxical aspect of money is evidence of its artistic nature. For, as Benjamin observes, works of art have historically been inseparable from their other functions, which were often magical or religious. The Renaissance opened the way for the triumph of the secular function of art, while the domination of society by capitalist relations brought the final demise of the ritual or cultic value of artworks. Art has become profane, detached from other functions, and even its rituals are largely secular. Yet money has never undergone the separation of functions that typifies art in late capitalism. Indeed, money could not be produced ‘as art’ and still remain money since its artistic aspect is an integral part of its functioning that flows from its ‘moneyness’. For this reason, money is a throwback to art in its primordial form; it is a peculiar relic of a bygone era.

确切地说，艺术面向与货币其他维度不可分离，是因为货币根本上是植根于商品交换的经济现象。尽管货币在历史进程中取得了多种形式，在不同社会中的存在方式也千差万别，它始终是一般等价物，即价值的独立形式。货币是市场的精髓，无论这市场是古希腊的商站、大马士革的巴扎，还是芝加哥金属交易所。货币所积累的更广泛的符号及其他功能——随使用它的每个社会的特征而不同——都来自它根本的经济性质，即它封装价值关系的能力。宗教性的艺术形式能够褪去膜拜面向而保留纯粹的审美价值。但货币若褪去其经济面向，就不会保留任何艺术之维，因为它将变成无意义的物件。货币要成为艺术，就必须作为货币被生产，并且始终保有它的“货币性”。就此而言，当代货币是一种真正古老的艺术形式，是艺术与其他功能原初统一的实例——那时艺术与物件的多重目的不可分离。

To be precise, the impossibility of separating the artistic from the other dimensions of money is due to money being fundamentally an economic phenomenon rooted in commodity exchange. Despite the many forms that money has acquired in the course of history and its highly variable presence in different societies, it remains the universal equivalent, or the independent form of value. Money is the quintessence of markets, whether these are the emporia of the ancient Greeks, the bazaars of Damascus, or the Chicago Metal Exchange. The broader symbolic and other functions that money accrues – varying with the characteristics of each society deploying it – are due to its fundamentally economic nature, i.e. to its ability to encapsulate value relations. Religious forms of art are able to shed the cultic aspect, while retaining a purely aesthetic value. But if money shed its economic aspect, it would retain none of its artistic dimension because it would become a meaningless object. For money to be art, it must be produced as money, and it must retain its ‘moneyness’ throughout. In this regard, contemporary money is a truly ancient form of art, an instance of the original unity of the artistic and other functions when art was inseparable from the multiple purposes of its objects.

与货币类似的东西可以在东正教会的圣像中找到：那是作为神之符号化而生产出来的美丽物件。在东正教圣像中，艺术的世俗面向与膜拜面向并不分离。阿索斯山岩壁堡垒中的修士仍在创作杰出的样本，但他们并不是在从事“艺术”生产。与西方教会不同，对他们来说，圣像首先是允许与上帝交通的宗教物件。它当然必须有美，绘制它也有严格死板的规则，但创作艺术品并不是画师的目的。然而圣像仍然是高水准的艺术，对信徒尤其如此——圣像为他们打开一扇通往神的符号之窗。货币以其非宗教的、世俗的方式类似于圣像：它在严格规则下为僵硬的经济目的而被创造，却获得了一种与其经济运行不可分离的艺术价值。

An analogue with money can be found in the icons of the Orthodox Church, beautiful objects produced as symbolisations of the divine. There is no separation of the secular and the cultic aspect of art in Orthodox icons. The monks in the rocky fastnesses of Mount Athos still create outstanding specimens, but they are not engaged in producing ‘art’. Unlike the Western Church, to them an icon is first and foremost a religious object allowing communion with God. There must certainly be beauty to it, and there are strict and rigid rules on how to render it, but creating an artwork is not the purpose of the painter. And yet the icons remain art of a high calibre, particularly for believers for whom they open a symbolic window to the divine. In its profane and secular manner, money is similar to an icon: it is created for a rigid economic purpose under strict rules and attains an artistic value that is inseparable from its economic functioning.

zh: 3 商品货币的材料及其符号功能
en: 3 The Material of Commodity Money and Its Symbolic Function

children: 把货币确认为一种艺术形式，为考察本雅明与阿多诺所关心的问题提供了新路径；但首先有必要更仔细地看看货币是什么、它自身的形式如何发展。这两个问题长久以来困扰着经济理论；只需说明，本章采用的进路来自马克思的分析。

Identifying money as a form of art offers a fresh path to examining the issues that concerned Benjamin and Adorno, but it is first necessary to look more closely at what money is and how its own form develops. Both of these questions have long exercised economic theory; suffice it to say that the approach adopted in this chapter derives from Marx’s analysis.

货币是“一般等价物”，它随着“相对”价值形式与“等价”价值形式的辩证法在商品交换中展开而出现。极简地概括：在任何一笔交换交易中，主动发起交易的商品采取“相对”价值形式，从而在一定量的另一种商品中“表现”自己的价值，即在被动回应“相对”一方的“等价”中表现。随着交换变得普遍而经常，相对与等价的辩证法不断展开，最终导致一种商品被选中，所有其他商品都在它身上“表现”自己的价值（即把它变成“一般等价物”）。换句话说，货币的出现，是因为所有其他商品都拿出来与它交换出售，从而使它能够购买一般商品。一般等价物就是为所有其他商品独立代表价值的商品，或者说能够一般地购买的商品。

Money is the ‘universal equivalent’ which emerges as the dialectic of the ‘relative’ and the ‘equivalent’ forms of value is played out in commodity exchange. Summarising ruthlessly, in any exchange transaction, the ‘relative’ form of value is adopted by the commodity that actively initiates the transaction and thereby ‘expresses’ its own value in a quantity of the other commodity, i.e. in the ‘equivalent’ which passively responds to the ‘relative’. The dialectic of relative and equivalent unfolds as exchange becomes general and regular, eventually leading to one commodity becoming selected as that in which all others ‘express’ their value (i.e. make it into the ‘universal equivalent’). Put differently, money emerges as all other commodities are offered for sale against it, thus enabling it to buy commodities in general. The universal equivalent is the commodity that independently represents value for all others, or the commodity that can buy in general.
这一论证的关键在于：一般等价物是其他商品的创造物，是交换过程的自发结果。因此，货币获得了马克思所说的“形式上的”使用价值，它纯粹因交换过程而存在，附加在货币作为普通商品的其他使用价值之上：

Key to this argument is the idea that the universal equivalent is a creation of the other commodities; it is a spontaneous outcome of the exchange process. Consequently, money acquires what Marx calls a ‘formal’ use value,
which exists purely because of the process of exchange and is additional to money’s other use value as a plain commodity:
货币商品获得了二重使用价值。除了它作为商品的特殊使用价值（例如金可以用来补牙，是奢侈品的原料，等等）之外，它还获得了一种形式上的使用价值，产生于它特定的社会环境。

The money commodity acquires a dual use-value. Alongside its special use-value as a commodity (gold, for instance, serves to fill hollow teeth, it forms the raw material for luxury articles, etc.) it acquires a formal usevalue, arising out of its specific social circumstances.

货币的形式使用价值是它的规定性特征，等于它表现其他商品价值——从而购买其他商品——的能力。理解货币形式使用价值的一个有洞察力的途径，是当代经济学所说的“外部性的网络效应”。假设一些商品在单一商品中“表现”自己的价值；这样做就使其他商品也在同一种商品中“表现”价值变得更有利；这种单一商品越是这样执行职能，它充当一般等价物的能力就越强；于是它的“货币性”就越强。网络效应不可避免地反映商品交换过程的社会、制度与习俗特征，也反映实际被选为货币的那种商品的特殊属性。历史进程中被典型选中的商品，当然是金或银。

The formal use value of money is its defining feature, amounting to its ability to express the value of – and thus to buy – other commodities. An insightful way of comprehending the formal use value of money is through what contemporary economics calls ‘network effects of externalities’. Assume that some commodities ‘express’ their value in a single commodity; by so doing, they make it more advantageous for others also to ‘express’ their value in the same; the more the single commodity functions in this manner, the stronger becomes its ability to act as universal equivalent still further; hence the stronger becomes its ‘moneyness’. Network effects inevitably reflect the social, institutional and customary features of the process of commodity exchange, but also the specific features of the commodity actually chosen as money. The commodity typically chosen in the course of history is, of course, gold or silver.

由此直接可知：与阿多诺相反，“大众”不是价值辩证法的单纯玩物，而是能动地确立货币的本质。货币之所以是货币，是因为“大众”接受它为货币，按货币来使用它，并预期他人也同样接受它。货币建立在“大众”之间心照不宣的共识之上，建立在无言信任的基岩之上；反过来，货币的习常使用又强化了“大众”对“货币性”的默契。既然人人都预期货币能够购买，商品所有者就用货币表现价值，并接受货币。反过来，货币所有者能够给商品所有者提供适足的交换价值形式，但这只是因为预期其他商品所有者会继续在同样基础上接受货币。货币中被投入了社会可接受性，它由商品所有者个体地和集体地维持着，正是它使货币成为货币。

It follows immediately that, contrary to Adorno, the ‘masses’ are not mere playthings of the dialectic of value, but actively establish the essence of money. Money is what it is because the ‘masses’ accept it as money, deploy it as such, and expect others to accept it similarly. Money rests on an implicit common understanding among the ‘masses’, on a bedrock of unspoken trust; its customary use, in turn, strengthens the implicit understanding of ‘moneyness’ among the ‘masses’. Since all expect money to be able to buy, owners of commodities express value in money, and accept money. Owners of money, in turn, are able to give to owners of commodities an adequate form of exchange value, but only because other commodity owners are expected to continue receiving money on the same basis. There is social acceptability invested in money which is individually and collectively sustained by commodity owners and which makes money what it is.
社会可接受性也是货币艺术之维的背后原因。货币之所以能够符号化权力、宗教、财富乃至对生活的态度，是因为“大众”把一种来自共享态度、信念与知识的共同信任投入其中。这种默契信任依赖于货币具有标准化、易于辨认的形式。由此可知，当货币以铸币形式被机械复制时，默契信任的基础被拓宽了，货币的运行被加强了。同样可知，货币之所以能够是艺术，恰恰因为它没有“灵光”：观察和接受它的人对它即刻而直接地熟悉。

Social acceptability also lies behind money’s artistic dimension. Money is capable of symbolising power, religion, wealth and even an attitude toward life itself because the ‘masses’ invest in it a commonly held trust deriving from shared attitudes, beliefs and knowledge. This implicit trust depends on money having standardised and easily recognisable forms. It follows that when money is mechanically reproduced in the form of coin, the basis of implicit trust is broadened, and money’s functioning is strengthened. It also follows that money could be art precisely because it does not have an ‘aura’: those who observe and receive it are instantly and directly familiar with it.
在这方面有两个因素至关重要。第一是货币商品的材料，“大众”把它变成社会信任的容器，因此它必须表现出本真性、耐久性与可转移性。作为社会信任与可接受性的承担者，货币商品的材料也会成为货币符号权力的化身。于是，金本身获得了与艺术表达的直接关联。金色或金箔是中世纪基督教圣像画最典型的背景；金与银都是宗教艺术的经典材料；金是本雅明“灵光”一词的语言来源，也是宗教艺术作品中出现的金色光环——光轮——的来源。
金直接就是货币，因此金直接就是艺术。

Two factors are of paramount importance in this regard. The first is the material of the money commodity, which the ‘masses’ turn into a repository of social trust, and which must therefore exhibit authenticity, durability, and transferability. As the bearer of social trust and acceptability, the material of the money commodity would also become the embodiment of money’s symbolic power. Thus, gold per se acquires a direct association with artistic expression. Gold colour, or gold leaf, is the background par excellence of Christian medieval iconography; both gold and silver are the classic materials of religious art; gold is the linguistic source of Benjamin’s ‘aura’ as well as of the golden halo, the nimbus, that appears in works of religious art.
Gold is directly money and hence it is directly art.

第二是国家的认可印记，它在“大众”当中确认货币材料的社会可接受性。国家是凌驾性的社会实体，有权增强商品所有者之间自发产生的社会信任。国家通常把货币切成铸币，从而确认货币材料对价值的代表，并使之标准化。在铸币形式上，货币不可能有“灵光”，但必须有本真性——它必须带着国家权力的徽记，不能磨损，不能是伪币。此外，铸币上铭刻的图像必须属于其社会的意识形态与观念构造，人们才会信任并接受它。铸币因此能够直接符号化使用它的社会。即使被剪边、磨损或以其他方式败坏，铸币仍能穿越岁月，传达其社会不诚实的一面。

The second is the imprimatur of the state which validates the social acceptability of the material of money among the ‘masses’. The state is an overarching social entity with the power to augment the social trust spontaneously generated among commodity owners. The state validates the representation of value by the material of money by typically cutting money into coin, and thereby also standardising it. In its coin form, money cannot have an ‘aura’, but it must have genuineness – it must carry the insignia of state power, it must not be worn out, and it must not be counterfeit. The images inscribed on the coin, furthermore, must be part of the ideological and conceptual make-up of its society, if people are to trust and accept it. The coin is thereby capable of directly symbolising the society that deploys it. Even when it is clipped, rubbed or otherwise corrupted, the coin is still capable of conveying the dishonest side of its own society down the ages.

这两个因素都是商品货币作为艺术重现已逝社会的基础。在古典古代，希腊城邦银币上精美灵动的图像，让位于马其顿国王腓力二世的庄严面容，散发着君主权力与近乎神性的气息。他的儿子亚历山大大帝，尽管已完全升格为世界的统治之神，却似乎没有把自己的形象放上自己的铸币——他用从波斯国王那里夺来的金银大量铸造货币。不过，他确实使用了披着狮皮的赫拉克勒斯形象，从而为他的继业者开辟了道路：他们把自己的头像放上铸币，戴着阿蒙神的羊角、象鼻、狮皮以及形形色色的其他象征物。神王的象征体系对从亚历山大帝国征服中产生的希腊化诸王国的合法性至关重要，希腊化国王自然把亚历山大以及自己的形象铭刻在铸币上。自希腊城邦以来，世界已深刻改变，因此希腊化铸币把神性与对国王面部畸形的坚决写实的表现巧妙地混合在一起。到了罗马帝国时代，世界改变得更为深刻：由神性加持的国家权力，通过坚实、精工、威严而呆板的铸币投射出来，就像罗马人的桥梁与渡槽。而拜占庭世界还有什么比金索利都斯——诺米斯玛——更生动的表现呢？它在最深沉的中世纪支配着货币交易，一面是神圣秩序之首基督，另一面是人居世界（oikoumeni）之首皇帝。

Both factors are fundamental to commodity money recreating as art the society that gave birth to it. In classical antiquity, the delicate and playful images of the silver coinage of Greek city-states gave way to the grave mien of King Philip ii of Macedon, exuding monarchical power and near divinity. His son, King Alexander the Great, despite having fully risen to the status of divine ruler of the world, appears not to have placed his image on his own coins, which he cut in abundance from gold and silver seized from the Persian kings. Nonetheless, he did use the image of Heracles wearing the lion skin, thus opening the way for his epigoni to place his head on their coins wearing the horns of Ammon, the proboscis of an elephant, the lion skin and a host of other symbolic objects. The symbolism of the god-king was vital to the legitimacy of the Hellenistic kingdoms that emerged from Alexander’s imperial conquests, and Hellenistic kings naturally inscribed Alexander’s as well as their own image on their coins. The world had changed profoundly since the Greek city-states, and thus Hellenistic coins nicely mixed divinity with resolutely realistic representations of the facial deformities of the king. The world had changed even more profoundly in imperial Roman times when state power backed by divinity was projected by coins that were solid, wellmade, authoritative and dull, like the bridges and aqueducts of the Romans. And what could be a more vivid representation of the Byzantine world than the gold solidus, the nomisma, dominating monetary transactions in the deepest Middle Ages, with Christ, the head of the divine order, on one side, and the Emperor, the head of the oikoumeni, on the other?

zh: 4 发达资本主义中货币的非物质化：货币作为层叠符号
en: 4 The Dematerialisation of Money in Advanced Capitalism: Money as Layered Symbol

children: 在发达资本主义中，货币已变得与历史上的铸币明显不同，因为它非物质化了，而它对国家认可印记的依赖如果说有什么变化的话，是变得更强了。于是，塑造货币可接受性与符号运行的这两个要素走上了十分不同的道路，对货币在当代世界的艺术之维有重大意涵。商品货币甚至已在形式上不再是流通与支付手段，退入少数中央银行保管的庞大贮藏之中。
它不再直接扮演货币角色，而是充当价值与财富的终极化身，由国家保管的最后屏障式贮藏。对负担得起的人来说，金也仍然是私人贮藏，是这个深深不确定的世界中一小块确定性的岛屿。

In advanced capitalism, money has become distinctly different from historic coin because it has become dematerialised, while its reliance on the imprimatur of the state has, if anything, become stronger. Thus, the two elements that shape the acceptability and the symbolic functioning of money have followed very different paths, with major implications for money’s artistic dimension in the contemporary world. Commodity money has ceased even formally to be a means of circulation and payment, retreating into vast hoards kept by a few central banks.

It no longer plays a direct monetary role, but acts as the ultimate embodiment of value and wealth, a hoard of last resort kept by the state. Gold also remains a private hoard, a small island of certainty in a deeply uncertain world, for those who can afford to keep it.
这条道路上的重大一步，是货币采取纸片——券——的形式。它仍是物理材料，但与金根本不同，因为它实际上没有价值。直觉上可知，让一张无价值的纸成为货币所需的社会信任，是另一个数量级的。然而，在这个相当明显的论点之外，分析必须小心从事，才不会迷失对资本主义货币运行至关重要的那些关系。因为与纸片相联系的货币有两种不同类型，它们赋予货币的符号与艺术权力十分不同的面貌。

A major step along this path was for money to assume the form of a paper slip – a note – which remains a physical material but is fundamentally different from gold since it is effectively valueless. It is intuitive that the social trust necessary for a valueless piece of paper to become money is of a different order of magnitude. Beyond this rather obvious point, however, the analysis must tread carefully if it is not to lose track of relations that are fundamental to the functioning of capitalist money. For there are two distinct types of money associated with paper slips, which lend a very different aspect to money’s symbolic and artistic power.

第一种是法定货币（fiat money），由国家直接发行，用它支付自己的开支，或接受人们用它缴税。这是一种无价值货币形式，在18世纪充分出现，并随着法国大革命的指券而引人注目。请注意，法定货币的出现是交换过程本身诱致的，并不是国家的任意行为。商品货币在流通中自然会损失一些材料——由于磨损、擦落等等——于是铸币自然地变得低于它所宣称的东西。实际上，铸币符号化自身。因此，商品货币不仅代表价值、符号化自己的社会，还开始符号化自身。法定货币是国家创造的商品货币的正规符号，国家利用了交换本身产生的符号化空间；它建立在国家以其选择的货币形式进行支付和接受支付的权力之上。简言之，发达资本主义中的非物质化货币，催生了基于国家权力与社会信任的层叠符号化与关系表象，同时达到了商品货币无法想象的复杂性。

There is, first, fiat money, which the state issues directly, using it to pay for its own expenditures, or receiving it in payment of taxes. This is a form of valueless money that emerged fully in the eighteenth century and attained prominence with the Assignats of the French Revolution. Note that the emergence of fiat money has been induced by the process of exchange itself and was not an arbitrary act of the state. Commodity money naturally loses some of its material as it circulates – due to abrasion, rubbing off, and so on – and thus coin becomes naturally less than the thing it proclaims itself to be. In effect, coin symbolises itself. Commodity money, therefore, not only represents value and symbolises its own society, but also begins to symbolise itself. Fiat money is a proper symbol of commodity money created by the state which takes advantage of the room for symbolisation generated by exchange itself; it rests on the state’s power to make and to receive payments in the form of money it chooses. Dematerialised money in advanced capitalism, in short, gives rise to a layered symbolisation and representation of relations based on state power and social trust, while attaining complexity unimaginable for commodity money.

第二种是信用货币，由私人金融机构（典型的是银行）在发放信用时发行，例如最初的银行券。这也是一种无价值货币形式，在18世纪变得引人注目——世纪初约翰·劳的银行实验闹得沸沸扬扬，而世纪末英国银行的实践则稳健得多。信用货币不是商品货币的符号，而是资本主义企业（银行）发行的私人支付承诺。换句话说，信用货币代表价值，但不符号化货币商品。信用货币成为货币所需的网络效应，远为依赖发行银行的信誉而非国家权力，这也是它在发达资本主义中成为主导货币的基础。

There is also, second, credit money, which is issued by private financial institutions (typically banks) as they advance credit, e.g. the original banknote. This is also a form of valueless money that became prominent in the eighteenth century, notoriously so in John Law’s bank experiment at the beginning of the century, but far more solidly by English banks toward the end. Credit money is not a symbol of commodity money, but is rather a private promise to pay issued by a capitalist enterprise (a bank). Put otherwise, credit money represents value but does not symbolise the money commodity. The network effects required for credit money to become money depend far more on the creditworthiness of issuing banks than on the power of the state, and that is also the basis on which it becomes the dominant money in advanced capitalism.

信用货币天生无价值，因为它只是私人支付承诺，靠被“大众”普遍接受而成为货币。它最引人注目的特征，是其形式随非物质化推进而变幻不定。信用货币的最初形式，即私人银行券的形式，很快被抛在后面，其他无价值、非物质化的形式出现了，典型地与银行存款相联系——存款仍是银行的支付承诺。信用货币很快表现为账簿条目、电报信号、电子信号，等等。它的进一步非物质化并无神秘之处，因为私人发行者的支付承诺不必存在于纸上或别的有形形式中，才能确保使用者接受它。要紧的是对发行者兑现承诺之能力的信任。于是，随着信用体系在发达资本主义中发展，信用货币成为完全非物质化的独立价值代表。

Credit money is inherently valueless since it is a mere private promise to pay which becomes money by being generally acceptable to ‘the masses’. Its most striking feature is the protean variability of its form that goes together with its advancing dematerialisation. The original form of credit money, i.e. that of the private banknote, is soon left behind as other valueless and dematerialised forms emerge, typically associated with bank deposits, which remain promises to pay by a bank. Credit money soon appears as book entries, telegraphic signals, electronic signals, and so on. There is no mystery in its further dematerialisation, since the promise to pay by the private issuer does not have to exist on paper, or in another corporeal form, to ensure its acceptability by those who use it. What matters is trust in the issuer’s ability to meet the promise made. Thus, as the credit system develops in advanced capitalism, credit money becomes a completely dematerialised independent representative of value.

然而，私人发行者实际承诺交付的是什么呢？在最抽象的层面上，银行显然承诺支付充当最终清算手段的货币商品。但在发达资本主义中，货币商品从流通中消失，最终支付手段变成了法定货币：银行承诺支付国家发行的法偿。最终支付手段实际上由中央银行创造，中央银行有国家撑腰，与私人银行进行信用交易。国家授予中央银行银行券发行垄断，保留了一些基本的物质性。尽管如此，法偿的绝大部分完全非物质化，采取私人银行在中央银行存款的形式。中央银行在向银行发放信用时创造银行券与存款，两者都保留支付承诺的形式，即信用货币的原初形式。然而，凭中央银行货币唯一能索兑的东西，就是它自身。当代法偿具有空洞的自我指涉形式——它实际上就是法定货币。

What, though, is actually promised to be delivered by the private issuers? At the most abstract level, a bank obviously promises to pay the money commodity which acts as the final means of settlement. However, in advanced capitalism, the money commodity disappears from circulation and the final means of payment becomes fiat money: a bank promises to pay legal tender issued by the state. The final means of payment is actually created by the central bank which has the backing of the state and engages in credit transactions with private banks. Some elemental materiality is retained as the state awards to the central bank a monopoly of banknote issue. Nonetheless, the great bulk of legal tender is completely dematerialised and takes the form of deposits held by private banks at the central bank. The central bank creates banknotes and deposits as it advances credit to banks, both of which retain the form of a promise to pay, i.e. the original form of credit money. Yet the only thing that could be claimed in exchange for central bank money is itself. Contemporary legal tender has an empty self-referential form – it is, in reality, fiat money.

价值的这一系列表象与符号化，以及货币在发达资本主义中非凡演化所需的层层信任，也塑造着货币的艺术之维。在银行券形式上——即通常掌握在个人手中的货币流通的小头——货币保留了铸币的一些有形性，也保留了铸币以图画形式再现社会权力、仪式与信念的能力。正如铸币在历史上所做的那样，银行券在资产阶级社会中也这样做， 尤其是通过捕捉民族认同的面貌。银行券既是民族认同的杠杆，也是它的证明；它之所以能在民族市场上获得可接受性，部分正在于反映了共享的历史文化背景。民族象征、文化信念与民众偏见在银行券上获得可见形式，从而促成可接受性所需的即刻辨认。那是何等沉重的表象，通常满载民族成就的图像——英雄、战役与伟大的心灵！不过，与过去的社会不同，发达资本主义的货币大体世俗化，因此把宗教主题排除在图像之外。

The series of representations and symbolisations of value, and the successive layers of trust necessary for the extraordinary evolution of money in advanced capitalism, also shape money’s artistic dimension. In the form of the banknote – i.e. the small end of money circulation typically found in the possession of individuals – money retains some of the corporeality of coinage as well as coin’s ability to reproduce the power, rituals, and beliefs of a society in pictorial form. As coin has done historically, so does the banknote in bourgeois society, above all, by capturing the outlook of national identity. The banknote is both lever and proof of national identity, an object that gains acceptability in the national market partly by reflecting a shared historical and cultural background. National symbols, cultural beliefs and popular prejudices are given visible form on the banknote, thus facilitating immediate recognition necessary for acceptability. And what ponderousness of representation, typically laden with the images of national achievement – heroes, battles, and great minds! Still, unlike past societies, advanced capitalist money is largely secular and thus excludes religious themes from its imagery.

符号化的层叠始于铸币金属实体的损耗——它使铸币符号化自身——在当代银行券上只会更加致密。法定货币是商品货币的正规符号，是凭国家一句话就在商品世界流通的冒名者。一旦开始作为货币流通，它自然也开始符号化其他关系，典型的是任何货币形式都能符号化的那些关系， 尤其是民族信念与偏见。对已经符号化金的法定货币来说，这是第二阶符号化；可以说是建立在符号主义之上的符号主义。一种虚假与人为的感觉弥漫在它的使用中，那是一层脆弱与假扮的织物，与“黄色金属”的坚实相距霄壤。如果国家发行失当，导致恶性通货膨胀，当代国家发行银行券的“货币性”就会崩溃——这一现象在20世纪已深深烙入民众记忆。当代艺术家承认银行券所执行的层叠而岌岌可危的符号化，于是在自己的作品中再现它的图像：这是艺术用艺术来加深符号化。同样，艺术家制作“假”银行券，即错视画（trompe-l'oeil）银行券，以凸显资本主义社会核心的假扮与权力关系；艺术伪币是在真实货币与符号货币的差异上做文章，因而也是在当代货币交换的脆弱性上做文章。

The layering of symbolisation, which starts with the erosion of the coin’s metallic substance that makes the coin symbolise itself, only grows denser with contemporary banknotes. Fiat money is a proper symbol of commodity money, an impostor circulating in the world of commodities on the say-so of the state. Once it starts to circulate as money, it naturally begins to symbolise other relations too, and typically those which any form of money would be capable of symbolising, above all, national beliefs and prejudices. For fiat money, which already symbolises gold, this is a second order of symbolisation; it is, as it were, symbolism built on symbolism. A sense of falseness and artifice pervades its use, a tissue of fragility and make-believe that is poles apart from the solidity of the ‘yellow metal’. The ‘moneyness’ of the contemporary state-issued banknote would collapse if the state mishandled its issue, leading to hyperinflation, a phenomenon that has been seared in popular memory in the twentieth century. Contemporary artists have acknowledged the layered and precarious symbolisation performed by the banknote, thus reproducing images of it in their own work: a case of art using art to deepen symbolisation. Similarly, artists have produced ‘fake’, or trompe-l’oeil banknotes to highlight make-believe and power relations at the heart of capitalist society; artistic counterfeits are a play on the difference between real and symbolic money, and thus on the precariousness of contemporary monetary exchange.

当代货币完全非物质化时，符号化的层叠达到顶点，同时也揭示了一切货币艺术内容的基础。账簿条目与电子转账形式的私人信用货币，是一种独立代表价值的非物质存在，因此能够抽象地符号化成熟资本主义的伦理与道德品质。铸币与银行券的图画面向被抛在一旁，金属或纸的材料也被抛在一旁，凸显出来的是纯粹的“货币性”，它符号化权力、信念、社会地位以及市场的无情搏杀（cut-and-thrust）。计算机屏幕上的一串符号在技术上是先进而真实的，同时又是非物质而符号性的。它把价值的抽象世界与具体世界合而为一，让资本主义社会干瘪的心脏清晰可见。在一个以前所未有的规模生产图像、并把艺术交给整理和操纵这些图像以生成意义、内容与情感的任务的世界里，货币的非物质化形式凸显了货币纯粹的艺术之维。非物质化货币因此是已变得自我反思、概念化的当代艺术的天然成分。

The layering of symbolisation reaches a peak when contemporary money becomes fully dematerialised, thus also revealing the foundation of the artistic content of all money. Private credit money in the form of book entries and electronic transfers is an immaterial presence that independently represents value and is thus capable of abstractly symbolising the ethical and moral qualities of mature capitalism. The pictorial aspects of coin and banknote are cast aside, together with the material of metal or paper, bringing to the fore pure ‘moneyness’ that symbolises power, belief, social standing and the ruthless cutand-thrust of the market. A series of signs on a computer screen is technologically advanced and real, while also being immaterial and symbolic. It elides the abstract and the concrete worlds of value, rendering visible the arid heart of capitalist society. In a world that produces images as never before and which has consigned art to the task of ordering and manipulating these images to generate meaning, content and sentiment, the dematerialised form of money brings to the fore the pure artistic dimension of money. Dematerialised money is thus a natural ingredient of contemporary art that has become self-reflexive and conceptual.
非物质化货币离本雅明的“机械复制”很远。银行券当然是“机械复制”的，而且必然没有“灵光”，因为它们必须让人即刻熟悉，才能确保所需的社会信任。到了完全非物质化的货币，“复制”本身的含义消失了，但这种货币代表价值的能力丝毫未减，作为艺术运行的力量也丝毫未减。由此可知，塑造货币为艺术的，不是“机械复制”本身，而是资本主义关系——正如比格尔在更一般地讨论本雅明分析时正确指出的那样。
然而，这方面更深的论点仍属于本雅明：“大众”直接地、通过反复接触——即以“消遣”的方式——把握非物质化货币，从而把信任投入其中。考察货币、“大众”与艺术之间关系的基础，至此已更充分地奠定。

Dematerialised money is a long way from Benjamin’s ‘mechanical reproduction’. Banknotes are certainly ‘mechanically reproduced’ and they necessarily have no ‘aura’ since they must be instantly familiar to ensure the required social trust. When it comes to completely dematerialised money, the very meaning of ‘reproduction’ disappears, but such money is no less capable of representing value and no less powerful in functioning as art. It follows that it is not ‘mechanical reproduction’ per se, but rather capitalist relations that shape money as art, as Bürger rightly observed in a more general discussion of Benjamin’s analysis.

And yet, the deeper point in this regard still belongs to Benjamin: the ‘masses’ come to apprehend dematerialised money directly and through repeated exposure – i.e. in ‘distracted’ fashion – thus investing it with trust. The ground is set more fully to examine the relation between money, the ‘masses’, and art.

zh: 5 货币在社会与艺术中的意识形态和拜物教
en: 5 The Ideology and the Fetishism of Money in Society and in Art

children: “大众”是“货币性”的创造者，因而是货币艺术内容的创造者，因为他们通过交换实践确立了货币的社会可接受性。然而资本主义是阶级社会，因此货币也结晶了价值所固有的剥削与压迫的阶级关系。就此而言，货币的艺术之维也在于它能够表现和符号化人类精神的堕落，表现和符号化一个屈从于资本逻辑的社会中人的价值、感知与情感的丧失。分析的问题在于：这些表象与符号化如何随货币的特定形式而变化，尤其在货币非物质化之际。在这方面货币有两个不同的面向，即意识形态与拜物教。

The ‘masses’ are the creators of ‘moneyness’, and thus of the artistic content of money, since they establish the social acceptability of money through the practice of exchange. Capitalism, however, is a class society and thus money also crystallises class relations of exploitation and oppression that are intrinsic to value. In this regard, the artistic dimension of money also resides in its ability to represent and symbolise the degradation of the human spirit, the loss of human values, perceptions, and sentiments in a society that has succumbed to the logic of capital. The issue for analysis is the manner in which these representations and symbolisations vary with particular forms of money, especially as money is dematerialised. There are two distinct aspects of money in this respect, namely ideology and fetishism.

意识形态是马克思主义政治理论与文化哲学的圣杯，尽管它与货币的联系仍然晦暗。与其陷入相互竞争的分析的泥潭，不如重温马克思本人对宗教的讨论，因为它与货币有平行之处。正如比格尔指出的，对马克思来说，宗教意识形态是“虚假意识”，即把人的品质、情感与自我认知投射到一个想象的实体上。然而宗教并不是任意产生的意识形态，因为它建立在阶级社会的压迫经验之上，甚至起到缓和不公之苦、平息反叛的作用。宗教或许可以称为“必要的意识形态”，其虚假性与它的功能角色无关。

Ideology is the holy grail of Marxist political theory and cultural philosophy, though its connection to money remains obscure. Instead of entering the morass of competing analyses, it is useful to be reminded of Marx’s own discussion of religion, for it has a parallel with money. For Marx, as Bürger notes,

religious ideology is ‘false consciousness’, i.e. the projection onto an imaginary entity of human qualities, sentiments and self-perceptions. Yet religion is not an ideology that has arisen arbitrarily, since it rests on the oppressive experience of class society and even serves the purpose of assuaging the bitterness of injustice and pacifying rebelliousness. Religion might be called a ‘necessary ideology’ whose falseness is irrelevant to its functional role.

资本主义社会中存在一种货币意识形态，在虚假性与必要性两方面都与宗教相似。就它把货币当作人类成就的缩影、在发达资本主义中助长一种独特的庸俗文化而言，它是“虚假的”。货币通常被视为社会地位的尺度、社会价值的证明、职业技能的量规，尤其是个人与家庭安全的担保。同样，货币被理解为审美判断的承保人、礼仪的制定者、伦理原则的供应商和正义的试金石。货币还被看作家庭与个人关系的枢纽，更不用说性关系借以折射的棱镜。它甚至是一切人类可钦佩之物的基准，证明纯洁、慷慨、同情与团结。英国人说，事物和人“像金子一样好”（good as gold）；美国人打趣说，感觉像“百万美元”（a million dollars）。最后，货币还预示民族认同的品质：通常的看法是，“强国——强币”。

There is an ideology of money in capitalist society that is similar to religion in both its falseness and necessity. It is ‘false’ insofar as it treats money as the epitome of human achievement, fostering a distinctive culture of vulgarianism in advanced capitalism. Money is commonly taken as the measure of social position, the proof of social worth, the gauge of professional skill, and not least as the guarantor of personal and familial security. Equally, money is understood as the underwriter of aesthetic judgement, the setter of manners, the purveyor of ethical principles and the touchstone of justice. Money is also seen as the pivot of family and personal relations, not to mention the prism through which sexual relations are reflected. It is even the benchmark for all that is admirable in humanity, attesting to purity, generosity, compassion and solidarity. Things and people are ‘good as gold’, as the English say, or feel like ‘a million dollars’, as the Americans quip. Money, finally, betokens the qualities of national identity: ‘Strong country – strong money’, as the common perception runs.
货币意识形态是“虚假意识”，但也是资本主义社会底层现实的真实反映。齐美尔观察到，货币是“社会区隔”的摧毁者，消灭古老传统的社会分化方式，代之以现金占有。
资本主义社会确实把它的伦理、审美、情感乃至道德准则建立在货币之上；而围绕民族市场组织起来的资本主义经济，也确实通过其货币的相对价值与其他经济体发生关系。把货币视为一切美德、情感、关系与概念之尺度的意识形态认知，并不是想象的虚构——仿佛只要指出来，人们就会去寻找人类交往的更深原则。
资本主义世界的经济、社会与政治生活确实被货币的普遍性所塑造，这对失去货币渠道的个人、或货币在世界市场上崩溃的民族来说，立刻变得显而易见。这一粗粝的现实反映在货币意识形态中，后者反过来又加强货币的社会可接受性，帮助使货币成为货币。货币无论以物质形式还是非物质形式，都符号化这种弥漫资本主义社会的狭隘意识形态。

The ideology of money is ‘false consciousness’ but also a true reflection of the underlying reality of capitalist society. Simmel observed that money is the destroyer of ‘social distinction’, eliminating ancient and traditional modes of social differentiation and replacing them with cash possession.

Capitalist society genuinely grounds its ethical, aesthetic, emotional, and even moral precepts on money, while a capitalist economy, organised around a national market, truly relates to other economies through the relative value of its money. The ideological perception of money as the measure of all virtues, feelings, relations and concepts is not a figment of the imagination which, if it were only pointed out, would lead to a search for deeper principles of human intercourse.

Economic, social and political life in the capitalist world is indeed shaped by the universality of money, as becomes immediately apparent to the individual who loses access to money, or to the nation whose money collapses in the world market. This brute reality is reflected in the ideology of money, which in turn strengthens the social acceptability of money, helping to make money what it is. Money, in both its material and dematerialised form, symbolises this narrow ideology that permeates capitalist society.
另一方面，附着于货币的拜物教代表着一组完全不同的关系。弗洛伊德认为，拜物教由意识到母亲没有阴茎而诱发，这种意识与某个物件或身体的一部分相联系，使之成为性刺激的容器。
拜物教是一种缺失的表达，导致性欲结晶到某个物上。相比之下，对马克思来说，商品拜物教是资本主义经济最深层运行的意识形态总括。
商品拜物教的产生，根本上是因为商品的价值不直接、也不可能直接表现为它之所是，即抽象人类劳动。毋宁说，在交换过程中，一种商品（相对方）的价值必然表现在另一种商品（等价方）的物体上。价值必然表现为一定量之物（另一种商品），而不是比如说劳动小时；当那个物成为货币时，价值就取得了独立形式。

Fetishism attached to money, on the other hand, represents an entirely different set of relations. Freud considered fetishism to be induced by the realisation of the lack of a penis in the mother which becomes associated with an object, or a part of the body, turning it into a repository of sexual stimulation.

Fetishism is an expression of an absence that leads to the crystallisation of sexual desire onto a thing. In contrast, for Marx, commodity fetishism is an ideological summation of the deepest workings of the capitalist economy.

Commodity fetishism emerges fundamentally because the value of a commodity does not and cannot appear directly as what it is, i.e. as abstract human labour. Rather, in the process of exchange, the value of one commodity (the relative) is necessarily expressed in the body of another (the equivalent). Value necessarily appears as a quantity of a thing (another commodity) instead of, say, hours of labour, and it attains an independent form when that thing becomes money.
马克思在批判蒲鲁东引入“劳动货币”以废除剥削的提议时所做的思想实验，可以让人洞察商品拜物教的根源。

对马克思来说，如果价值要直接表现为抽象劳动小时（即“劳动货币”），就必须有一个凌驾性机构（也许是一家国家银行），以一致的方式计算社会必要劳动，同时考虑劳动生产率的变化和总供求构成的变动。这样，价值内容就会以社会有效的方式为一切经济活动参与者所知。但这样一来，同一个机构也会被迫监督和管理它已计算出价值的产品的交换，包括劳动力。这种事态自然会压制或排除市场， 结果将是一个不再是资本主义的社会。由此可知，在仍然保持资本主义的经济中，商品价值必然要表现在物上，货币必然要代表一般价值，充当价值尺度、交换与支付手段、价值贮藏手段。货币必须是资本主义经济的记录与记忆装置，是把物质事物与过程黏合在一起的胶水，是标记资源转移的信号，是重新平衡生产力的工具。简言之，像资本主义这样天生碎片化的社会，必然依赖价值的独立形式充当经济的无意识组织者。

Insight into the roots of commodity fetishism can be gained from the mental experiment undertaken by Marx in a critique of Proudhon’s proposal to introduce ‘labour money’ as a way of abolishing exploitation.

For Marx, if value were to be expressed directly as hours of abstract labour (i.e. as ‘labour money’), it would be necessary to have an overarching agency (perhaps a national bank) that would calculate socially necessary labours in a consistent way, taking into account the changing productivity of labour and the shifting composition of aggregate demand and supply. Value content would then be known in a socially valid way by all participants in economic activity. But then, the same agency would also be led to supervise and manage the exchange of products whose value it would have calculated, including labour power. Such a state of affairs would naturally suppress or exclude the market, and it would result in a society that was no longer capitalism. It follows that in an economy that remains capitalist, commodity value necessarily has to be expressed in things, and money has to represent value in general, acting as measure of value, means of exchange and payment, and store of value. Money has to be the recording and memory device of a capitalist economy, the glue that brings material things and processes together, the signal that marks the transfer of resources, and the instrument that rebalances the productive forces. In short, an inherently fragmentary society such as capitalism necessarily relies on the independent form of value to act as the unconscious organiser of the economy.

然而价值根本上是人与人之间的社会关系。首先，它是生产者在一定财产与其他制度框架内对产品的关系；其次，它是生产者通过交换产品相互接触时对其他生产者的关系；最后，它是商品所有者对受雇生产该商品的劳动者的关系。当价值表现为另一种商品（而不是抽象劳动），并最终由货币独立代表时，这一整套复杂的社会关系——包含财产与权力——就从视野中消失了。从事经济活动的人之间的关系，被归摄于商品与货币的关系之下。生产者的劳动从视野中消失，被推到概念前台的量是价格、货币量、生产成本，等等。构成“经济”的那些物，被人类感知为塑造生活的支配力量。

Value, though, is fundamentally a social relation among human beings. It is, first, a relation of the producer toward the product within a given framework of property and other institutions; it is also a relation of the producer toward other producers as they come into contact with exchange products; it is finally a relation of the owner of the commodity toward the labourers employed in its production. This complex set of social relations – incorporating property and power – vanishes from sight when value is expressed as another commodity (rather than as abstract labour) and comes eventually to be represented independently by money. Relations among human beings engaged in economic activity become subsumed under relations of commodities and money. The labour of producers vanishes from sight and the magnitudes that are propelled into conceptual prominence are prices, quantities of money, production costs, and so on. The things that constitute ‘the economy’ are perceived by humanity as the dominant forces that shape life.

因此，商品拜物教不是“虚假意识”，而是世界实际所是的反映。一个人可以充分理解商品拜物教的荒谬，起来反抗价格、利息率、利润率之类，却丝毫不能减少拜物教。一个有意识的主体可以充分意识到，让货币这样一个物来塑造人的生活是怪诞的，但货币仍将继续是组织资本主义经济的物一样的主体。这一点在债务关系中最为明显——债务是当代资本主义的显著特征——在债务中，货币表现为支配家庭与个人生活的外在力量，因为它当然确实就是这样一种力量。货币拜物教的荒谬内建于经济、社会乃至生活本身的结构之中。

Commodity fetishism is, thus, not ‘false consciousness’, but a reflection of how the world actually is. An individual could fully comprehend the absurdity of commodity fetishism and rebel against prices, rates of interest, rates of profits, and the like, without reducing fetishism one jot. A conscious subject might fully realise that it is bizarre to have money as a thing shaping human lives, but money would continue to be the thing-like agent organising the capitalist economy. Nowhere is this more evident than in relations of debt, a salient feature of contemporary capitalism, in which money appears as an external force dictating the lives of households and individuals because, of course, it truly is such a force. The absurdity of the money fetish is built into the structure of economy, society and life itself.

与阿多诺相反，商品拜物教不是交换价值的胜利，也不是一切的无情商品化。恰恰相反，商品拜物教实际上建立在物之上，即建立在使用价值之上。资本主义的驱动动机是价值的自我膨胀及其作为货币利润的积累，但资本主义从未完全摆脱使用价值。它的核心是粗陋的唯物主义，表现在技术、组织方法与供给体系上，更不用说由技能、年龄、习惯与消费偏好构成的劳动力。拜物教就是这些物质现实仿佛学会说价值语言的过程，形成表现为成本、价格与各种比率的关系。物质现实由此支配人与人之间作为工人、资本家、家户成员乃至最终作为个人的关系。与此同时，生活的物质面向开始通过交换价值的范畴被感知，这些范畴随之把社会关系遮蔽于视野之外。商品拜物部分地居住在物质这一侧。

In contrast to Adorno, commodity fetishism is not the triumph of exchange value, nor is it the relentless commodification of everything. On the contrary, commodity fetishism actually rests on things, i.e. on use values. The driving motive of capitalism is the self-expansion of value and its accrual as money profit, but capitalism never breaks completely free of use value. There is crass materialism at its heart, which is expressed in technologies, methods of organisation, and systems of provision, not to mention a labour force comprising skills, ages, habits and consumption preferences. Fetishism is the process whereby these material realities, as it were, learn to speak the language of value, forming relations expressed as costs, prices and various rates. Material realities thereby dominate relations among human beings as workers, capitalists, householders and ultimately as individual persons. At the same time, the material side of life comes to be perceived through the categories of exchange value, which then obscure social relations from view. The fetish of the commodity resides in part on the side of the material.

这种拜物教弥漫于新古典经济学：它只关注物与物的关系，忽视经济现象根部的社会关系，并给它的粗陋唯物主义披上冒充科学的技术魔法外衣。同样明显的是嵌入流行经济观念中的拜物教，例如认为失业可能上升、生活条件可能恶化，是因为“经济”“表现不好”。拜物教关乎生活的物质面向充当价值的容器，价值在货币中拥有自己的独立形式，并接管生活的伦理、道德、情感与审美面向。它关乎人类在“经济”的“客观”力量面前所谓的无能为力。粗陋唯物主义开始在思想中统治，也在日常生活中统治。然而它之所以统治，是因为日常生活资本主义之下本来就是粗陋物质的。

Such fetishism permeates neoclassical economics which focuses exclusively on relations among things, ignoring the social relations that lie at the root of economic phenomena, and dressing its crude materialism in a cloak of technical wizardry that pretends to be science. Similarly apparent is the fetishism embedded in commonly held economic views, for instance, that unemployment might rise and living conditions might worsen because ‘the economy’ is ‘doing badly’. Fetishism is about the material side of life acting as the repository of value with its own independent form in money, and taking over the ethical, moral, emotional, and aesthetic side of life. It is about the putative helplessness of humanity in the face of the ‘objective’ forces of the ‘economy’. Crude materialism comes to rule in thought, but also in everyday life. Yet it rules because everyday life is crudely material under capitalism.
货币是商品拜物教的承担者与执行者——不是它的符号。在其物质存在中，无论是金还是银行券，货币都是拜物教的物理化身，是具体封装物对人的统治的材料。艺术作品中使用实物货币，使拜物教的荒谬现实具体化（无需符号化）——因此它直接而即刻就是艺术。

随着货币非物质化，拜物采取了无身体的形式，变得抽象而一般，因而更具社会性，因为它被封装在一组账簿条目或电子信号中。尽管如此，非物质化货币继续组织资本主义经济，而中央银行以总体理性管理这种货币，在一个无计划的世界里充当计划者。对中央银行来说，终极目标是促进资本主义企业的营利，“经济”是它的参照域。中央银行服从一种直接铭刻在指导社会货币的社会与技术实践中的拜物。这是一种接管成熟资本主义的“理性拜物”，一种直接由非物质化货币承担的拜物，即由组织经济运行的无身体社会存在所承担的拜物。

Money is the bearer and agent of commodity fetishism – not its symbol. In its material presence, be it gold or a banknote, money is the physical embodiment of fetishism, the material that concretely encapsulates the rule of things over human beings. Physical money deployed in works of art makes concrete (without symbolisation) the absurd reality of fetishism – it is thus art immediately and directly.

As money becomes dematerialised, the fetish takes a disembodied form, it becomes abstract and general and thus more social, since it is encapsulated in a set of book entries, or electronic signals. Nonetheless, dematerialised money continues to organise the capitalist economy, while the central bank manages this money with aggregate rationality, operating as a planner in an unplanned world. For the central bank, the ultimate aim is to foster the profit-making of capitalist enterprises, and the ‘economy’ is its field of reference. The central bank conforms to a fetish that is inscribed directly in the social and technical practices that guide society’s money. It is a kind of ‘rational fetish’ that takes over mature capitalism, a fetish borne directly by dematerialised money, i.e. by a disembodied social presence that organises the functioning of the economy.
那么，“大众”在成熟资本主义中如何回应货币拜物？齐泽克——援引佐恩-雷特尔——声称，商品所有者像“实践上的唯我论者”那样行事，即他们无视交换的社会语境，却始终意识到自己在按个人利益行事。他们在自身内部“压抑”交换的社会维度，盲目地、无意识地把价值辩证法作为“实在”抽象演出来。于是，商品形式的“虚假”意识形态成了有意识主体的一部分，这个主体在以“唯我论者”身份执行交换时“意识形态地”行动着。
And how do the ‘masses’ respond to the fetish of money in mature capitalism? Zizek – drawing on Sohn-Rethel
– claimed that commodity owners act as ‘practical solipsists’, that is, they ignore the social context of exchange but remain conscious of operating in their personal interest.

They ‘repress’ the social dimension of exchange within themselves, and blindly, or unconsciously, act out the dialectic of value as a ‘real’ abstraction. Thus, the ‘false’ ideology of the commodity form becomes part of the conscious subject who acts ‘ideologically’ while performing exchange as a ‘solipsist’.

齐泽克说价值的抽象是“实在的”，这没错，因为它是资本主义经济中实际发生的经济过程；但他把有意识主体看作不把握社会语境而演出抽象的“唯我论者”，这种看法是不充分且误导的。商品所有者预期货币具有社会可接受性，因而预期他人普遍也有同样预期。在这方面存在意识的共同性，它直接就是社会性的，很大程度上因为它建立在相互承认的符号化之上。同样，商品所有者预期他人普遍分享货币意识形态，即使那是“虚假意识形态”。尤其是，商品所有者通过服从经济互动的物质号令而演出拜物教，而拜物教根本不是“虚假意识形态”。这些物质号令通常被感知为外在力量，即“经济”的“客观现实”。因此连拜物教也是被社会性地把握的——不存在对围绕交换的共同偏见一无所知、只关注个人利益的“唯我论”主体。例如，人们共同担忧“通货膨胀”这种限制获取工资品的外在力量，若不是这种社会性把握，又是什么呢？

Zizek is right that the abstraction of value is ‘real’, insofar as it is an economic process actually occurring in a capitalist economy, but his view of the conscious subject as a ‘solipsist’ acting out the abstraction without apprehending its social context is inadequate and misleading. Commodity owners expect money to have social acceptability, and thus expect others generally to have the same expectation. There is a commonality of consciousness in this respect that is immediately social, not least because it is based on mutually recognised symbolisations. Similarly, commodity owners expect others generally to share the ideology of money, even if that is ‘false ideology’. Not least, commodity owners act out fetishism, which is not at all ‘false ideology’, by submitting to the material dictates of economic interaction. These material dictates are commonly perceived as external forces, the ‘objective reality’ of the ‘economy’. Thus even fetishism is socially apprehended – there is no ‘solipsistic’ subject that is ignorant of the common prejudices surrounding exchange and focusing exclusively on personal interests. What else, for instance, is the common concern with ‘inflation’ as an external force that restricts access to wage goods?

有意识主体始终意识到货币对私人生活与社会生活的支配面向，很大程度上因为正是主体的行动把必要的可接受性注入货币。“大众”在资本主义进程中意识到自身的堕落，并不是资本均质化力量的被动、“唯我论”或盲目的容器。正因如此，货币不服从是发达资本主义的特征性现象，催生了大量替代性货币形式——绿色美元、时间货币，等等。这些货币形式依托自觉努力排除资本统治的共同体与结社关系，在当代资本主义内部不断涌现。它们符号化拒绝资本、寻求替代性社会组织形式的做法与态度，无论这些渴望多么不成形。反叛精神在“大众”中没有死去，希望正在于此。

The conscious subject remains aware of the dominating aspect of money over private and social life, not least because the actions of the subject inject the necessary acceptability into money. The ‘masses’ realise their own degradation in the course of capitalism and are not passive, ‘solipsistic’ or blind receptacles of the homogenising force of capital. This is why monetary insubordination is a characteristic feature of advanced capitalism, resulting in a profusion of alternative forms of money – green dollars, time money, and so on. Drawing on communal and associational relations that consciously strive to exclude the rule of capital, such forms of money continually emerge within contemporary capitalism. They symbolise practices and attitudes that reject capital and seek alternative forms of social organisation, no matter how inchoate these yearnings may be. The spirit of rebellion has not died among the ‘masses’, and therein lies hope.
